answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to prove a fresh VDF: repeated modular squaring links every step to the prior result, so a clone cannot skip ahead or divide one chain among GPUs. An atlas of identities may run separate chains in parallel, but each still incurs its own sequential wall-clock delay; even quartz-fast hardware cannot remove it. A verifier checks the compact Wesolowski proof, while the signal of costly elapsed computation raises the price of cloning.
